questions.question: A model answers a question about last week's news from its built-in knowledge alone. What should you expect?
choices: The knowledge may be stale because pre-training has a cutoff
It will retrieve an exact news archive
Post-training guarantees current facts
The context window updates model weights
questions.explain: Pre-training is costly and infrequent, so recent information generally requires a tool such as search.

questions.question: What happens when you press Enter in a chat?
choices: The model replaces the conversation history
Control passes to the model, which adds tokens to the shared sequence
The app retrains the model on your prompt
The context window is cleared
questions.explain: A chat grows as user and model take turns appending tokens to the context window.

questions.question: Why is the 'lossy zip file' analogy useful?
choices: It means the model stores every page word for word
It describes compressed, probabilistic knowledge rather than an exact archive
It means the model can unzip websites when asked
It describes only the chat interface
questions.explain: Pre-training compresses patterns from internet text into parameters, so recall is approximate rather than exact.

questions.question: Which question is most suitable for the model's built-in knowledge, based on the lesson's rule?
choices: What happened in a city this morning?
What is a widely discussed, longstanding fact?
What is the current price of a stock?
What are today's revised safety rules?
questions.explain: Built-in recall is most promising when information is both old and common across the internet.

questions.question: The model gives a specific ingredient list for a medicine. What is the best next step if accuracy matters?
choices: Assume it is right because the product is popular
Check the package or an authoritative primary source
Ask the same model to repeat it
Treat the answer as a medical diagnosis
questions.explain: The lesson treats model output as fallible recollection and verifies product details against the box.

questions.question: How should verification change when the stakes rise?
choices: Use less verification because the model will be cautious
Scale checking to the stakes and verify high-impact claims carefully
Verify only if the answer sounds unusual
Never use models for low-stakes questions
questions.explain: The lesson recommends calibrating verification effort to the consequences of being wrong.

questions.question: Your conversation shifts from planning a trip to debugging code. What is the recommended move?
choices: Keep every trip detail in the same chat just in case
Start a new chat and carry over only relevant information
Ask the model to forget the last turn but keep the rest
Switch models without changing context
questions.explain: A topic switch is a good time to reset the context window so irrelevant tokens do not clutter the task.

questions.question: Why can a very long, unrelated chat hurt performance?
choices: Old context can distract the model and increase sampling work
The model permanently forgets its training
The app deletes its tools
Long chats always change the selected model
questions.explain: The context is working memory; stale tokens can distract and make responses slower or costlier.

questions.question: When should useful earlier context stay in a conversation?
choices: Always, no matter the topic
Only when it is genuinely relevant to the current task
Never; every message should be isolated
Only when the chat is short
questions.explain: The advice is to remove irrelevant context while retaining information the current task needs.

questions.question: Before relying on an answer for work, what should you check in the chat app?
choices: The active model and what your plan includes
Only the app's logo
Whether another tab is open
The number of old conversations
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes checking the model selector and the plan's actual limits and access.

questions.question: Why might a provider charge more for a larger model?
choices: It costs more compute to run
It always uses a browser
It stores more chat history
It has fewer parameters
questions.explain: Larger models require more computation, which is why providers commonly charge more for access.

questions.question: You use an LLM occasionally for casual tasks. How should you choose a tier?
choices: Automatically buy the most expensive tier
Pick the least costly option that meets your needs, then reassess
Assume free access is always the flagship
Choose based on the provider's name alone
questions.explain: The talk recommends making the cost and capability trade-off based on your own use.

questions.question: A routine writing task is handled well by the regular model. What is the lesson's suggested default?
choices: Switch to a reasoning model for every prompt
Stay with the regular model unless the task needs more reasoning
Use the largest model regardless of task
Ask the regular model to pretend it reasoned longer
questions.explain: Try without reasoning first and escalate when the task is not being solved adequately.

questions.question: Which task is the clearest candidate for a thinking model?
choices: Choosing a greeting
Solving a difficult multi-step math problem
Reformatting a short list
Repeating a sentence
questions.explain: Reasoning models are presented as especially useful for math, code, and complex reasoning.

questions.question: What does the lesson say thinking models add?
choices: A guarantee of truth
More deliberate reasoning that can improve accuracy on hard tasks
Automatic access to the internet
A larger context window in every app
questions.explain: The talk describes reinforcement-trained reasoning models as an accuracy boost for demanding problems, not a guarantee.

questions.question: You need a reliable update about a story from today. Which approach fits the lesson?
choices: Use a search tool to bring fresh information into the conversation
Rely on the model's training cutoff
Start a longer chat so it recalls the news
Ask for a more confident tone
questions.explain: Recent facts are not reliably in model weights, so search can supply up-to-date material.

questions.question: Why isn't search automatically available in every chat?
choices: Browsing is a tool that the app or model must provide
Search is part of every context window
The model refuses all recent questions
Search only works in voice mode
questions.explain: The base model is self-contained; internet search is an added tool and not every app offers it.

questions.question: After a search-enabled answer gives an important claim, what is a sound practice?
choices: Inspect the supporting sources and verify high-stakes details
Ignore sources because search guarantees correctness
Assume every result is official
Disable context for the rest of the chat
questions.explain: Search provides fresh information, but claims still benefit from source checking, especially when stakes are high.

questions.question: You have a broad question that needs evidence gathered across many sources. What does a deep-research tool help with?
choices: Conducting a more extended, source-based investigation
Changing the model's training data
Guaranteeing every source is correct
Replacing the need to define the research question
questions.explain: Deep research is presented as a tool for undertaking broader research and synthesizing information from sources.

questions.question: How can you make a research request more useful?
choices: State the question, scope, and what evidence or comparison you need
Say only 'research everything'
Ask it to skip citations
Hide relevant constraints until the end
questions.explain: A clear scope and decision need help guide the research process toward relevant evidence.

questions.question: A deep-research report supports a consequential decision. What should you do?
choices: Review its cited sources and check key claims
Trust the report because it is long
Use only its conclusion paragraph
Assume citations mean the sources agree
questions.explain: Research synthesis can still err, so verify the underlying sources for important conclusions.

questions.question: You want an LLM to answer questions about a paper you provide. What is the useful role of an upload?
choices: It places the document's contents into reach for analysis in the chat
It permanently retrains the model on the paper
It proves every statement in the paper is true
It automatically makes the paper public
questions.explain: An uploaded document gives the model material to work with in the current task; it does not retrain the model.

questions.question: A long book exceeds what the chat can handle at once. What is a sensible workflow?
choices: Work from relevant sections or chunks and check answers against the text
Keep uploading unrelated files until it works
Ask for page numbers without giving source context
Assume the model has memorized the whole book
questions.explain: Large documents may need focused sections, and answers should remain grounded in the supplied source.

questions.question: The model summarizes an uploaded source with a suspicious quote. What should you do?
choices: Check the quote in the original document
Assume file uploads eliminate hallucinations
Ask for a more certain summary
Delete the source immediately
questions.explain: Providing a file helps ground the response but does not remove the need to verify exact details.

questions.question: You need to calculate a result from a large table of numbers. Why use a Python interpreter tool?
choices: It can execute computation instead of relying on guessed arithmetic
It adds the table to pre-training
It guarantees the input data is correct
It searches the web automatically
questions.explain: A Python tool lets the model run code for calculations rather than simulate arithmetic from memory.

questions.question: The computed answer seems wrong. What is the best debugging step?
choices: Inspect the code, inputs, and assumptions
Trust it because code ran
Switch to voice mode
Ask for a more confident number
questions.explain: An interpreter can execute code accurately while still using incorrect data, code, or assumptions.

questions.question: Which request most clearly benefits from a Python tool?
choices: Compute statistics across thousands of rows
Explain a common phrase
Suggest a conversation starter
Rewrite one short sentence
questions.explain: Programmatic tools are useful when a task involves substantial or repeatable computation.

questions.question: You upload data and want a plot plus summary statistics. What can Advanced Data Analysis add?
choices: A Python-backed workflow for analyzing data and producing figures
A guarantee that columns are labeled correctly
Automatic knowledge of the data's real-world source
A way to change the model's personality globally
questions.explain: Advanced Data Analysis combines uploaded data with executable analysis such as calculations and plots.

questions.question: A chart looks polished, but the conclusion seems surprising. What should you inspect?
choices: The data, transformations, and code or assumptions behind the chart
Only the chart colors
Whether the file name is short
The model's writing style
questions.explain: A data tool can help analyze and visualize, but results depend on inputs and analytic choices.

questions.question: Which is a better analysis prompt?
choices: Ask for a specific comparison and explain what each column means
Say 'make insights' with no context
Ask it to invent missing rows
Request a graph without saying what matters
questions.explain: A defined question and data context help the tool choose relevant analyses and visualizations.

questions.question: You want to sketch a small interactive web app while discussing an idea. Which feature fits this use?
choices: Claude Artifacts
A model memory manager
A Python interpreter alone
A custom instruction field
questions.explain: Artifacts are highlighted for inline prototyping of simple web apps and diagrams.

questions.question: What is a useful way to iterate on a generated diagram?
choices: Describe the structure or change you want and refine the artifact
Treat the first version as guaranteed final
Ask a search tool to change its layout
Add unrelated context to the chat
questions.explain: Artifacts support interactive prototyping, so clear revision requests help shape the result.

questions.question: You are choosing an app for a simple diagram prototype. What principle does the talk recommend?
choices: Choose tools by their strengths, since different apps may lead in different niches
Use only one provider for every task
Pick whichever has the highest price
Assume all apps have identical features
questions.explain: The talk describes a competitive ecosystem where particular apps can excel at specific jobs.

questions.question: You are building software professionally and want an AI-centered coding environment. What tool does the talk point to?
choices: Cursor with Composer
NotebookLM
Advanced Voice
A memory bank
questions.explain: Cursor and Composer are identified as tools for professional programming work.

questions.question: An AI-generated code change is large. What should you do before relying on it?
choices: Review and run the code in the project context
Assume generated code is correct
Only ask the model to praise its own solution
Ignore errors because it is vibe coding
questions.explain: AI coding helps produce changes, but the resulting code still needs inspection and validation.

questions.question: Why provide a coding assistant with project context and a clear task?
choices: It helps the assistant make changes that fit the actual codebase goal
It guarantees all bugs disappear
It gives the model current web access
It increases the model's training data
questions.explain: Relevant instructions and context help coding tools produce work aligned with the project.

questions.question: When might voice input be more convenient than typing?
choices: When speaking a thought or question is faster or more natural
When the task requires exact code punctuation
Whenever the model needs internet access
When you want a new chat to keep old context
questions.explain: Voice can make conversational input easier, while the underlying task still determines whether it is suitable.

questions.question: A voice transcription mishears a key name or number. What should you do?
choices: Correct the transcript or restate the detail before acting on the answer
Assume speech recognition is perfect
Ignore the detail because audio is multimodal
Ask the model to remember it permanently
questions.explain: Voice systems can misrecognize speech, so consequential details should be checked and corrected.

questions.question: What is a practical benefit of spoken model output?
choices: You can listen and interact conversationally without reading every response
It makes answers inherently more factual
It removes the need for context
It enables the model to know private facts
questions.explain: Audio output changes how you consume a response, not whether its content is automatically true.

questions.question: What makes an advanced voice experience feel more conversational?
choices: Low-latency spoken back-and-forth that can handle natural turn-taking
A long delay before every reply
Only converting finished text into audio
A separate chat for every sentence
questions.explain: Advanced voice is presented as a more direct, natural spoken interaction with the model.

questions.question: You need to discuss a nuanced topic by voice. What should you remember?
choices: Voice convenience does not remove the need to check important claims
Spoken answers are always more accurate
The model can hear facts that were never provided
Voice mode guarantees a human expert
questions.explain: The voice interface changes the modality of interaction, not the model's fallibility.

questions.question: A voice feature is missing from your phone app. What is a reasonable explanation to check?
choices: Feature availability can differ between web and mobile platforms
The model has forgotten how to speak
Your account's context window is full
Voice features are identical everywhere
questions.explain: The talk notes that features may differ between a web interface and a mobile app.

questions.question: You want to turn a collection of provided sources into a podcast-like discussion. What is NotebookLM's demonstrated role?
choices: Generating an audio overview from source material
Searching every current website by default
Training a new foundation model
Saving global chat personality settings
questions.explain: NotebookLM is shown as a way to create podcast-style audio from selected source material.

questions.question: Why provide relevant sources before generating an audio overview?
choices: The output should be grounded in the material you want discussed
It guarantees the audio has no errors
It makes sources unnecessary to review
It gives the tool access to private files automatically
questions.explain: Source material supplies the basis for the generated discussion and helps focus its coverage.

questions.question: The generated podcast summarizes a technical claim. What should a careful listener do?
choices: Check the claim in the underlying source
Assume a conversational format guarantees accuracy
Ignore source details because audio is easier
Treat it as a primary research paper
questions.explain: An audio summary is still generated content, so important claims should be verified against the source.

questions.question: You want help interpreting a chart in a screenshot. What should you do?
choices: Provide the image and ask a specific question about it
Describe it only as 'look at this'
Assume the model can see files you did not attach
Ask a text-only model to search your device
questions.explain: Image input lets a multimodal model inspect visual material when it is supplied in the conversation.

questions.question: A screenshot contains tiny text that matters to your question. What is prudent?
choices: Provide a clear crop or transcribe the critical text, then verify the reading
Assume every pixel is read perfectly
Ask for a confident guess
Convert it to audio
questions.explain: Visual interpretation can miss details, especially small text, so improve the input and verify key readings.

questions.question: What does multimodal image input mean in practice?
choices: The system can use image content alongside the text prompt
The model knows every image on the internet
The image changes the model's training weights
All images are automatically public
questions.explain: Image input adds visual content as another modality for the model to interpret with the prompt.

questions.question: You want a visual concept rather than a written description. What can image generation do?
choices: Create an image from a prompt, sometimes with reference images
Guarantee exact text rendering in every image
Retrieve the original file from training
Turn a still image into verified evidence
questions.explain: Image-generation tools produce visuals from instructions and may use references to guide the result.

questions.question: The first generated image is close but misses the desired composition. What is a useful next step?
choices: Refine the prompt with concrete visual changes
Assume the model cannot be iterated
Ask for unrelated factual citations
Change custom instructions globally
questions.explain: Specific prompt revisions can steer visual output toward the composition you want.

questions.question: Why should you inspect a generated image before using it?
choices: Generated details may be inconsistent or differ from the request
Image generation always copies a source exactly
The prompt guarantees every detail
Inspection retrains the generator
questions.explain: Generated visuals can contain mistakes or unexpected details, so review them for the intended use.

questions.question: You provide a clip and ask what changes over time. What does video input contribute?
choices: Visual frames and temporal context from the supplied clip
Automatic access to every camera on your device
A guarantee of perfect audio transcription
New facts in the model's training
questions.explain: Video input gives the model visual material from a clip to analyze, subject to the tool's capabilities.

questions.question: A key event happens briefly in a long clip. How can you improve the question?
choices: Point to the relevant time range or provide a focused excerpt
Ask a vague question about the whole video
Assume every frame is equally important
Request a current web search instead
questions.explain: Focusing the model on the relevant segment makes the requested analysis clearer and more manageable.

questions.question: The model describes a small object incorrectly in a clip. What is the sensible response?
choices: Check the relevant frames yourself and clarify the object
Assume video analysis is infallible
Ask it to invent a clearer frame
Treat the description as a verified fact
questions.explain: Multimodal interpretation can miss visual details, so verify consequential observations against the clip.

questions.question: You want a short animated scene with a particular subject and camera movement. What helps guide video generation?
choices: Describe the scene and motion clearly, and use a reference when useful
Provide only a file extension
Assume the model will infer your unstated style
Ask for a transcript
questions.explain: A clear description of content and motion gives the generator direction; references can further guide it.

questions.question: A generated clip has the right subject but the wrong motion. What should you revise?
choices: Specify the desired action, timing, or camera movement more concretely
Only increase confidence wording
Ask a separate model to remember the clip
Remove all visual details
questions.explain: Video prompts benefit from explicit motion and camera guidance, not just a subject description.

questions.question: Before publishing an AI-generated clip, what should you do?
choices: Review the output for visual artifacts and whether it matches the brief
Assume each frame is physically consistent
Use it without watching because the prompt was clear
Treat it as recorded documentary evidence
questions.explain: Generated video can have inconsistencies, so inspect the actual result before using it.

questions.question: What is the difference between chat context and the memory feature described?
choices: Context belongs to a conversation; saved memory can be prepended to later chats
They are the same and both reset every turn
Memory stores every word of every chat
Context is a separate permanent user database
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes the current chat's context from a separate memory bank that persists across chats.

questions.question: You want the assistant to remember a durable preference. What can you do?
choices: Ask it to remember the preference, then review it in memory settings
Repeat it in every unrelated prompt forever
Assume every detail is saved automatically
Put it only in a temporary chat
questions.explain: The feature may save useful information, and the lesson recommends explicitly asking or managing memory entries.

questions.question: A saved memory is outdated. What is the appropriate action?
choices: Edit or delete it in the memory manager
Start a new chat and assume it disappears
Keep it because memory is immutable
Change the model tier
questions.explain: Memory entries are manageable text that can be viewed, edited, added, or deleted.

questions.question: You want every conversation to use a direct, educational tone. Where should that preference go?
choices: Custom instructions
A single temporary prompt
A file upload in each chat
The model selector
questions.explain: Custom instructions are global settings for how the assistant should respond across conversations.

questions.question: Why should you put only durable preferences in custom instructions?
choices: They apply globally between conversations
They are erased after each message
They change only one answer
They automatically update model weights
questions.explain: Because instructions affect future chats broadly, they are best suited to preferences you want applied repeatedly.

questions.question: You want a particular formality level when practicing a language. What is a useful instruction?
choices: Specify the register you want as a default
Ask for random tone changes
Save each sentence as a custom GPT
Rely on the model to infer your preference every time
questions.explain: The lesson uses language-learning formality as an example of a durable preference to state explicitly.

questions.question: You repeatedly ask for vocabulary in the same format. What is a good reason to make a custom GPT?
choices: Save the reusable prompt so each session needs only new input
Train a new model from scratch
Get guaranteed access to every tool
Store all your chats permanently
questions.explain: The lesson describes custom GPTs as saved prompts that reduce repeated setup work.

questions.question: What tends to make a reusable task prompt more reliable?
choices: Include concrete examples of the desired input and output
Use a vague one-line instruction only
Remove all task context
Ask the model to guess the format
questions.explain: Few-shot examples show the model the pattern and can improve accuracy over a bare description.

questions.question: A custom GPT is giving inconsistent translations. What should you improve?
choices: Clarify the task steps and add representative examples
Give it a more impressive name
Ask it to be confident
Remove instructions and rely on defaults
questions.explain: The lesson recommends clear task specifications plus examples, which teach the reusable pattern.

questions.question: You need fresh information, a difficult calculation, and a simple prototype. Which mapping matches the talk's checklist?
choices: Search for fresh facts, Python for calculations, Artifacts for a prototype
Memory for current news, voice for calculations, search for the prototype
A larger context for all three
Custom instructions for all three
questions.explain: The summary maps search to fresh information, Python to computation, and Artifacts to app or diagram prototyping.

questions.question: A regular model solves your task well. What is the recommended escalation strategy?
choices: Keep it; try a reasoning model if the task is not being solved
Always use reasoning mode first
Switch to a different app every turn
Buy the top tier immediately
questions.explain: The talk recommends trying without reasoning first, then escalating for harder problems if needed.

questions.question: You cannot find a feature on mobile that you saw on the web. What should you consider?
choices: Feature availability can differ by platform
The feature must have been removed everywhere
The model's training is incomplete
The context window is too short
questions.explain: The summary warns that web and mobile versions may not offer identical features.
